_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for V retrospectives (retro/build_v.py), generated from Visa Inc.'s own filings: every raw figure is the row string it appears in (kept in 'rows'), checked against its filing, and every growth rate, margin, gap and rule-T value is computed from those figures. Every value is tied to a source and becomes visible only on or after that source's 'published' date (EDGAR's acceptance time; after the 16:00 ET close, the next trading day). Dollar figures in millions as the filings print them ('_m'; the Visa U.S.A. statements in thousands are stored divided by 1,000); per-share figures as published, the class A common stock's.

history_vintages.why: 'Visa operates the world’s largest retail electronic payments network and manages the world’s most recognized global financial services brand.' 'The global payments industry depends heavily upon the overall level of consumer, business and government spending.' 'Within the general purpose payment card industry, we face substantial and intense competition worldwide.'; no 10-K calls the business cyclical (the economy and spending are a 'why', not the company's own label: the LOW, SHW and JPM reading), so the kind is DURABLE; no disruption theme in taxonomy_eras.json is live for a payments network on these dates, so the watch list is empty

eps_first_excluded.2008: a distorted year with no figure excluding only one-offs: GAAP $0.96 a diluted class A share (FY2008 10-K) carries the $1,457M covered-litigation reserve (the Q4 FY08 release's reconciliation; $1,470M litigation provision), about $874M after the year's 40% GAAP tax rate against $804M of net income, so reported EPS is under half the EPS without it (the AAPL FY2002 test); the company's adjusted $2.25 also removes asset step-up amortization ('Non-cash amortization and depreciation of the incremental basis in technology and building assets acquired in the reorganization.', $68M a year), which recurs, applies 'a normalized tax rate of 41%' and counts the IPO shares as issued at October 1, 2007, so it does not exclude only one-offs (the NKE FY2007, AVGO and PFE rule); FY2008 is Visa Inc.'s first year with EPS ('There is no comparable earnings per share measure for 2007 as we were a non-stock company.'), so the history and the P/E window start after it (the ACN FY02 and JPM FY2002 rule): FY2009, from 2008-10-01

guide.note: the 11-15% range stands with its words 'at the lower end' in the note (the ACN words rule); EPS growth 'of greater than 20%' is a one-sided bound and gives no field (the PEP, UNP and LOW rule); the operating margin 'in the mid 50% range' is words and gives no step; incentives, advertising, tax, capital expenditure and free cash flow have no input in method r2

dividends.note: $0.105 a quarter, the first declared (8-K of 2008-06-11, after the close)
dividends.quote: SAN FRANCISCO, CA, June 11, 2008 – Visa Inc. (NYSE:V) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly dividend in the aggregate amount of $0.105 per share of Class A Common Stock (determined in the case of Class B and Class C Common Stock on an “as converted” basis) payable on August 29, 2008 to all holders of record of the Company’s Class A, Class B and Class C Common Stock as of August 15, 2008.
today announced that its Board of Directors had declared a quarterly dividend in the aggregate amount of $0.125 per share of class A common stock

revenue.measure: growth of total operating revenues (net of volume and support incentives), %

net_to_gross.measure: change in total operating revenues as a share of gross operating revenues (service, data processing, international transaction and other revenues before volume and support incentives), bp: the share of gross revenues kept after client incentives, in the place of the gross margin

opex_gap.measure: growth of operating expenses excluding the litigation provision line, less revenue growth, pp (lower is better)

receivables_gap.measure: growth of year-end accounts receivable less revenue growth, pp (lower is better), each pair of year ends from the latest filing published by 2009-10-29 whose balance sheet reports both (the S-4/A for 2005-2006, the 424B4 for 2006-2007, the FY2008 10-K for 2007-2008), with that filing's revenues

op_margin.measure: change in operating margin (operating income over total operating revenues, litigation provisions in, as published), bp

fiscal_calendar.rule: the fiscal year ends on September 30 (FY2009 = 2008-10-01 to 2009-09-30)
fiscal_calendar.quote: For the fiscal year ended September 30, 2008

price_basis: Yahoo's V series is the class A common stock, NYSE: V, from its 2008-03-19 listing; Yahoo adjusts it for the four-for-one split of 2015-03-19, which the builder undoes (retro_tool.split_factor), so every price the models use is the close as traded
